8 May 2026

Statement on Monetary Policy

Statement on Monetary Policy, May 2026.

Overview

Inflation is expected to return to the target range by 2026. GDP growth is expected to be 2.1 per cent in 2026.

Domestic economic conditions

The Australian economy grew at a moderate pace over the year.

The labour market

The unemployment rate is expected to be 4.4 per cent in 2026. Wage growth is projected to be 3.2 per cent in 2026.

Inflation and prices

CPI inflation is projected to average 2.8 per cent in 2026. Underlying inflation is expected to be 2.9 per cent in 2026.

Financial conditions

Financial conditions have tightened since the last Statement.

The stance of monetary policy

The Board decided to hold the cash rate.

Monetary policy will remain data dependent.

Risks

The risks to the inflation outlook are broadly balanced. Risks to growth are tilted to the downside.

Assumptions

Technical assumptions underpin the forecasts.

Reserve Bank of Australia, 2026
